attribution_limitations: The abstract describes a weeklong history of fatigue, nausea and flu-like symptoms; the case text states the fatigue and flu-like symptoms preceding the jaundice lasted five days. "Weeklong" is read as an approximation (ambiguity, not a source conflict); the case-text duration is carried on the accepted items and the abstract items stay review-only.
The text says hepatitis panel results suggest acute HAV and the conclusion calls it an acute HAV infection; whether cholecystitis was later excluded or confirmed is not stated.
The follow-up sentence says follow-up entailed counseling and ensuring resolution of jaundice and viral shedding without stating whether these were delivered.

The text describes the CT as gall bladder contraction with wall edema and mucosal hyper-enhancement; the Figure 1 caption describes gall bladder contraction with wall thickening. Different wording for the same CT, not a numeric conflict; both are kept as stated.

claims.text: A male in his early 30s presented to the emergency department with yellowing of the skin and sclera, fatigue, flu-like symptoms, nausea, tan-colored bowel movements, dark urine and subjective fevers, and denied abdominal pain, vomiting, diarrhea, hematuria and rashes. He took HIV prophylaxis medication, reported previous intravenous drug use with last use three years earlier, and had mild well-controlled asthma. He was hemodynamically stable, diffusely jaundiced, with scleral icterus and mild right upper quadrant tenderness.

claims.text: CT of the abdomen and pelvis showed gall bladder contraction with wall edema and mucosal hyper-enhancement without gallstones. Laboratory evaluation showed thrombocytopenia, hyperglycemia, hyperbilirubinemia, transaminitis and elevated PT-INR, which suggested possible new-onset diabetes mellitus and significant liver dysfunction. Cholecystitis and obstructive jaundice were suspected. MRCP showed no gallstones or biliary or pancreatic ductal dilatation. The hepatitis panel showed no HBV or HCV reactivity but was reactive for anti-HAV IgM, suggesting acute hepatitis A.
